November 12th, 1895

Somewhere only god knows.

I write this with a hand that trembles and a breath that comes like wind through torn sails. There is no one left to read this, yet I must write, if only to prove that we once lived.

I am Elias Morgan,last of the Black Heron.

The last of her crew.

The last of the hunted.

They found us, one by one.

We left Black Heron somewhere in the East nearby and hid

here. Now I'm the only one left.

They took Captain Hale and shot him in Eastern Coast.
Only he knew about the treasure. He always worried about going it to wrong hands.

Never thought some treasure would

Dive Log – 14th August 1978

Coordinates withheld. Depth: 112 meters.
Explorer: Dr.James Silva, Independent Oceanographic Surveyor

I am writing this from the research vessel Aquila.

I have seen things that should not exist, and yet they do ancient, waiting.

For decades, legends spoke of Thalor’s Hold, a palace of claims and tides, a seat of rulers who commanded the sea itself. Most historians

dismissed it as myth—Atlantis echoes, sailor superstition. But sonar found an anomaly: stonework patterns too symmetrical, too deliberate to be natural.

Inside, I found a stone tablet which seems to be some kind of message to the
visitors. But I couldn't translate it. And I never been to that place ever again.
